preparedBy: this repository, to test the evaluator
note: Six samples, one per locale and runtime stratum. Written here, by whoever wrote the rules, which is the one thing a holdout may not be — so evidenceClass says so and the evaluator refuses to call any number here P7 evidence. It is also far below the per-rule minimum on purpose: the refusal it earns is what the fail-closed test observes.

samples.summary: A cookie banner with one button. Accepting is offered and declining is not.
The same banner shape with both choices offered at equal weight. Built to look like the page above and must stay quiet.

A signup form whose marketing checkbox ships pre-checked, written as React's defaultChecked. The rule stays silent on it — issue #335 — and this label is kept rather than edited to match the output, which is the rule that makes a holdout worth having.
The same form with the same checkbox left unchecked. A near miss for the rule above.
A Figma export whose checkbox component carries Checked = true.
The same component with Checked = false. A near miss for the rule above.
